knowledge:
- key_parameters: method=In norm_tab(), specifies the normalization method ('total' for total sum scaling or 'raref' for rarefaction). In com_dis(), specifies the dissimilarity metric (e.g., 'bray' or 'tina'). In adj(), specifies the correlation method ('pearson' or 'spearman'). In net_cls(), specifies the clustering method ('mcl' or 'ap'). In net_dis() and net_dis_indi(), specifies the network distance metric ('spectra' or 'Jaccard') ;; depth=In norm_tab(), the target sequencing depth for rarefaction ;; multi=In norm_tab(), the number of bootstrap iterations for rarefaction to reduce random effects ;; sig=In adj(), logical indicating whether to perform a significance test for correlations. In bs_pm(), logical indicating whether to perform significance testing during bootstrap-permutation ;; cutoff=In net_cls(), the correlation threshold used to filter out weak connections before clustering ;; group=In bs_pm(), com_r2(), and get_r2(), the metadata column name(s) used to define sample groups ;; g_size=In bs_pm(), the minimum number of samples required per group; groups with fewer samples are discarded ;; s_size=In bs_pm(), the sub-sampling size for bootstrap and permutation (must be smaller than g_size, preferably less than half) ;; per=In bs_pm(), the occupancy threshold (percentage of samples) below which rare compositions are filtered out ;; bs=In bs_pm(), the number of bootstrap iterations ;; pm=In bs_pm(), the number of permutation iterations ;; individual=In bs_pm(), logical indicating whether to output bootstrap and permutation results separately to a directory to save memory ;; out_dir=In bs_pm() and net_dis_indi(), the directory path for storing or reading individual comparison results
- alternatives: tina()=Can be used directly on a normalized matrix instead of com_dis(method = "tina") to customize Spearman correlation, weighted Jaccard, multi-threading (threads), and block size (nblocks) ;; net_dis_indi()=Used instead of net_dis() to calculate network distances when bootstrap-permutation results were written to an external directory using individual = TRUE
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing metagenomic or taxonomic profiling datasets (such as OTU or ASV tables) to perform standard diversity analyses (alpha/beta diversity, PCoA) and extend them to co-occurrence network inference, network clustering, higher-order feature analysis, and statistical comparison of ecological networks across different environmental or biological conditions.
- pitfalls: The descriptive metadata table must contain a column named exactly 'Sample_ID' which matches the column names (sample identifiers) of the quantitative table ;; Mismatches between the quantitative and descriptive tables will cause errors; always run fit_tabs() to align them before downstream analyses ;; The bootstrap-permutation process (bs_pm()) is highly computationally intensive for large datasets; always pre-filter rare compositions using per and set appropriate g_size and s_size values ;; s_size must be strictly smaller than g_size, and ideally less than half of it, to ensure valid sub-sampling.

workflows.name: community_diversity_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform data normalization, calculate community dissimilarity, evaluate unexplained variance, and visualize beta-diversity using PCoA.
workflows.stages: 1. Create mina object and align tables ;; 2. Normalize data using total sum scaling or rarefaction ;; 3. Calculate community dissimilarity (e.g., Bray-Curtis) ;; 4. Calculate unexplained variance ratio ;; 5. Perform dimensionality reduction and plot beta-diversity
workflows.code:
library(mina)
    # maize_asv2 and maize_des2 are subset of maize_asv and maize_des
    maize <- new("mina", tab = maize_asv2, des = maize_des2)
    maize <- fit_tabs(maize)
    # check available normalization methods
    ? norm_tab_method_list
    # normalized by total sum
    maize <- norm_tab(maize, method = "total")
    # normalized by rarefaction
    maize <- norm_tab(maize, method = "raref", depth = 5000)
    # normalized by rarefaction and bootstrap 9 times
    maize <- norm_tab(maize, method = "raref", depth = 5000, multi = 9)
    # check available dissimilarity parameters
    ? com_dis_list
    # tidy the norm tab, intial tab and des tab
    maize <- fit_tabs(maize)
    # community dissimilarity calculation, Bray-Curtis used in example
    maize <- com_dis(maize, method = "bray")
    # get the unexplained variance ratio of quantitative table according to the
    # group information indicated in descriptive table.
    com_r2(maize, group = c("Compartment", "Soil", "Host_genotype"))
    # use tables as input
    maize_dis <- dis(maize)
    get_r2(maize_dis, maize_des, group = c("Compartment", "Soil", "Host_genotype"))
    # dimensionality reduction
    maize <- dmr(maize)
    # plot the community beta-diversity
    # separate samples from different conditions by color, plot PCo1 and PCo2
    p1 <- com_plot(maize, match = "Sample_ID", color = "Compartment")
    # plot PCo3 and PCo4
    p2 <- com_plot(maize, match = "Sample_ID", d1 = 3, d2 = 4, color =
                    "Compartment")
    # in addition, separate samples from different soil type by shape
    p3 <- com_plot(maize, match = "Sample_ID", color = "Compartment", shape =
                    "Soil")
    # plot PCo1 and PCo4
    p4 <- com_plot(maize, match = "Sample_ID", d1 = 1, d2 = 4, color =
                    "Compartment", shape = "Soil")

workflows.name: network_clustering_and_higher_order_analysis
workflows.intent: Infer co-occurrence networks, perform network clustering, generate higher-order feature tables, and analyze higher-order community diversity.
input: maize (mina object containing normalized quantitative data)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate correlation adjacency matrix ;; 2. Perform network clustering using MCL or AP ;; 3. Generate higher-order cluster table by summing member abundances ;; 4. Calculate dissimilarity and unexplained variance on the cluster table
workflows.code:
# check available adjacency matrix
    ? adj_method_list
    # Pearson and Spearman correlation
    maize <- adj(maize, method = "pearson")
    # Pearson and Spearman correlation with significance test
    maize <- adj(maize, method = "spearman", sig = TRUE)
    # check available network clustering methods
    ? net_cls_list
    # network clustering by MCL
    maize <- net_cls(maize, method = "mcl", cutoff = 0.6)
    # network clustering by AP
    maize <- net_cls(maize, method = "ap", cutoff = 0.6, neg = FALSE)
    # get the cluster table by summing up compositions of the same cluster
    maize <- net_cls_tab(maize)
    # dissimilarity between samples based on cluster table
    maize_cls_tab <- cls_tab(maize)
    maize_cls_dis <- com_dis(maize_cls_tab, method = "bray")
    get_r2(maize_cls_dis, maize_des, group = c("Compartment", "Soil",
                                               "Host_genotype"))

workflows.name: statistical_network_comparison
workflows.intent: Compare ecological networks across different sample groups and statistically assess their dissimilarity using bootstrap-permutation.
input: maize (mina object containing quantitative and descriptive data)
workflows.stages: 1. Align tables ;; 2. Run bootstrap-permutation to construct true and pseudo networks ;; 3. Calculate network distances (Spectral or Jaccard) ;; 4. Assess significance and extract distance statistics
workflows.code:
# compare the networks from different compartments
    maize <- fit_tabs(maize)
    maize <- bs_pm(maize, group = "Compartment")
    # only get the distance, no significance test
    maize <- bs_pm(maize, group = "Compartment", sig = FALSE)
    # set the size of group to remove consitions with less sample
    # also larger s_size will lead to more stable results but will consume more
    # computation and time resource
    maize <- bs_pm(maize, group = "Compartment", g_size = 200, s_size = 80)
    # remove the compositions appear in less than 20% of samples
    maize <- bs_pm(maize, group = "Compartment", per = 0.2)

    # set the bootstrap and permutation times. Again the more times bootstrap
    # and permutation, the more reliable the significance, with increased
    # computation and time resource.
    maize <- bs_pm(maize, group = "Compartment", bs = 11, pm = 11)

    # output the comparison separately to the defined directory
    bs_pm(maize, group = "Compartment", bs = 6, pm = 6,
    individual = TRUE, out_dir = out_dir)
    # check the available methods
    ? net_dis_method_list
    # calculate the distances between matrices
    maize <- net_dis(maize, method = "spectra")
    maize <- net_dis(maize, method = "Jaccard")
    # check the ditance results and significance (if applicable)
    dis_stat(maize)
    # the comparison stored separately in previous step
    ja <- net_dis_indi(out_dir, method = "Jaccard")
    dis_stat(ja)
    spectra <- net_dis_indi(out_dir, method = "spectra")
    dis_stat(spectra)
